explanation: Matches erdosproblems.com/455: for primes q_1 < q_2 < ⋯ with convex gaps q_{n+1} − q_n ≥ q_n − q_{n−1}, must q_n/n² → ∞? The Lean statement: for every strictly increasing q : ℕ → ℕ of primes with q(n+2) − q(n+1) ≥ q(n+1) − q(n) (natural subtraction is exact by monotonicity), q(n)/n² → ∞. Indexing from 0 rather than 1 shifts n by one, which does not affect the limit since n²/(n+1)² → 1. Faithful (positive form of the yes/no question).
